title: The shell comment reader gets its round-2 fixes: docstring, arithmetic cases, two false alarms and a wrong UNKNOWN
why: Round 2 of lane comment-check-scans-shell (PR #1834) passed with four findings left unfixed so the reviewed head stays put (lane, 02:05 CST Nov 8): (1) lint/check_comment_narration.py:19 docstring says "Every Python and Swift hit prints first", not "Python, Swift and shell"; (2) the `((` command form, the restore after a failed arithmetic read (lines 393-404) and the word state after a line continuation are unpinned, e.g. `(( x = 16#ff )) # c`, `(( n <<= 1 ))`; (3) false alarm: `[[ $x =~ ^(a)(#b)$ ]]` and extglob `+(a|b)#c)` read as comments, same family as the `esac)#` line in note comment-narration-limits; (4) wrong UNKNOWN: `a[1<<2]=x` is read as a heredoc and exits 2, same family as `let x=1<<2`.
note: Fix: correct the docstring; pin (2) with cases; fix (3) and (4) with a red case each and a control where a real comment and a real heredoc still read as such.
